title: Spiritual Tourism in Karnataka: Udupi, Dharmasthala, Shravanabelagola and Hampi

metaDescription: Plan a spiritual trip in Karnataka: Udupi, Dharmasthala, Kukke Subramanya, Sringeri, Kollur, Gokarna, Murudeshwar, Shravanabelagola and Bylakuppe, with routes.
description: A guide to spiritual tourism in Karnataka: Udupi's Krishna Matha, Dharmasthala, Kukke Subramanya, Sringeri's Sharada Peetham, Kollur Mookambika, Gokarna and Murudeshwar on the coast, Chamundi in Mysuru, the Hoysala temples, Hampi's Virupaksha, Shravanabelagola and the Tibetan monasteries of Bylakuppe, with coastal and hill routes.
dek: Karnataka's temple routes run along the coast and through the Western Ghats, with Jain and Buddhist sites alongside.

hero.alt: The ornate entrance of the Sri Krishna Matha at Udupi, Karnataka

intro: Karnataka's best-known pilgrim circuit follows the coast and the Western Ghats: Udupi's Sri Krishna Matha, Dharmasthala's Manjunatha temple, Kukke Subramanya, Sringeri's Sharada Peetham, the Mookambika temple at Kollur, and the sea-facing shrines of Gokarna and Murudeshwar.

Inland are Mysuru's Chamundi hill temple, the Hoysala masterpieces of Belur and Halebidu, Hampi's living Virupaksha temple, the Jain town of Shravanabelagola, and Bylakuppe's Tibetan monasteries, the largest Tibetan settlement in south India.
quickAnswer: Karnataka's main spiritual destinations are Udupi's Sri Krishna Matha, Dharmasthala, Kukke Subramanya, Sringeri, Kollur Mookambika, Gokarna and Murudeshwar on the coast, Chamundi hill in Mysuru, Hampi's Virupaksha temple, Shravanabelagola for Jains and Bylakuppe's Namdroling monastery. A coastal and Western Ghats temple route from Mangaluru takes about five to six days. October to March is the best time.
takeaways: The coastal temple route runs from Mangaluru through Udupi, Kollur and Murudeshwar to Gokarna.
Dharmasthala, Kukke Subramanya and Sringeri lie in the Western Ghats, reached on winding roads.
Shravanabelagola is a major Jain site; Bylakuppe is a major Tibetan Buddhist settlement.
Mysuru's Dasara (September or October) is the state's biggest festival.
October to March is best; the monsoon is heavy on the coast.

items.name: Udupi
body: The Krishna Matha, where the deity is viewed through a small window associated with the saint Kanakadasa, surrounded by the eight mathas founded by Madhvacharya.

image.alt: The Sri Krishna Matha in Udupi, Karnataka
image.caption: Sri Krishna Matha, Udupi

items.name: Dharmasthala and Kukke Subramanya
body: Two major Western Ghats shrines about 50 km apart. Dharmasthala's Manjunatha temple is administered by a Jain family and serves free meals to pilgrims.

items.name: Sringeri and Kollur
body: The Sharada Peetham at Sringeri, traditionally linked with Adi Shankaracharya, and the Mookambika temple at Kollur below the Kodachadri hills.

items.name: Gokarna and Murudeshwar
body: The Mahabaleshwar temple at Gokarna and Murudeshwar's giant seated Shiva on a headland.

items.name: Mysuru
body: Chamundeshwari temple on Chamundi hill, counted among the Shakti Peethas, and the Dasara festival.

items.name: Hampi
body: The Virupaksha temple is still in worship among the ruins of Vijayanagara.

items.name: Shravanabelagola and the Hoysala temples
body: Gommateshwara on Vindhyagiri, and the carved temples of Belur and Halebidu.

items.name: Bylakuppe
body: The Namdroling monastery's golden temple in a Tibetan settlement near Kushalnagar.

sections.heading: Stays and tips
list: Udupi and Mangaluru have the most hotels for the coastal route.
Dharmasthala and Kukke Subramanya have temple-run guesthouses as well as private lodges.
Many coastal temples require traditional dress for men, often a dhoti without a shirt, inside the inner shrine.
Temples in the Ghats are reached on winding roads; allow extra time and avoid night driving in the monsoon.

safety: Darshan waits vary from minutes to many hours; no one can guarantee quick darshan, so plan buffer time.
Dress modestly and follow each temple's rules on dress, phones and photography.
Coastal seas are rough in the monsoon; do not swim at Gokarna or Murudeshwar when flags are up.
Drive carefully on Ghat roads, especially in rain and fog.
packing: Dhoti or mundu for men; saree or long dress for women

faqs.q: Can I visit Hampi's Virupaksha temple?
faqs.a: Yes. It is still in active worship among the Vijayanagara ruins.

faqs.q: Which are the main temples in coastal Karnataka?
faqs.a: Udupi, Kollur Mookambika, Murudeshwar and Gokarna, with Dharmasthala and Kukke Subramanya inland.

faqs.q: How many days are needed for the Karnataka coastal temple tour?
faqs.a: About four to five days from Mangaluru.
Its Manjunatha temple is administered by a Jain family, and free meals are served to pilgrims.

faqs.q: Where is the Tibetan monastery in Karnataka?
faqs.a: At Bylakuppe near Kushalnagar, where the Namdroling monastery is known for its golden temple.

faqs.q: Is there a dress code at Udupi Krishna Matha?
faqs.a: Men are usually asked to remove shirts for some areas and rituals; follow the notices at the entrance.

faqs.q: How far is Sringeri from Udupi?
faqs.a: About 80 km, around two and a half hours through the Ghats.
In September or October; check the dates for the year.
